card.title: PlayStation 4 Standby Current Draw & Boot Sequence Analysis

claims.statement: Connect PIN 1 and PIN 4 of the 5Vstby connector to the positive terminal of a bench power supply set to +5V to monitor current draw during the standby boot sequence.
claims.evidence: The normal standby current sequence is 23mA, then 125mA, then 30mA.
claims.quote: Connect PIN 1 and 4 to the positive terminal of your power supply. Set the voltage to +5V and monitor the current draw. The normal boot sequence should be: 1e = 23mA 2e = 125mA 3e = 30mA

claims.statement: If current draw stays at 99mA with no boot, the southbridge may be bad or the 32Khz crystal is not oscillating.
claims.evidence: A 99mA stuck draw indicates a potential bad southbridge or missing clock signal.
claims.quote: If it stays at 99mA with no boot it could mean that the southbridge is bad. Check the 32Khz crystal if it oscillates. If the 32Khz signal is missing, then replace the southbridge clean flux of the board.

claims.statement: If current draw stays at 7mA with no boot, the southbridge is not working or failing to send a control signal to the transistor.
claims.evidence: A 7mA stuck draw points to southbridge control failure.
claims.quote: If it stays at 7mA with no boot it could mean that the southbridge is not working or sending a control signal to the transistor

procedure: Connect PIN 1 and PIN 4 of the +5Vstby connector to a bench power supply set to +5V.
Monitor current draw to verify the normal boot sequence stages (23mA, 125mA, 30mA).
Check the 32Khz crystal for oscillation if current draw is stuck at 99mA.

measurements.context: power good goes high after power button pressed

card.caveats: Stuck current draws are generalized indicators and require corroborating measurements.
